heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Overture PLA Professional seamlessly out of the box on its stock stainless steel nozzle without needing an enclosure. Running at a volumetric flow limit of 21 mm³/s allows reliable speeds up to 250 mm/s with exceptional layer adhesion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (clean with Isopropyl Alcohol or warm soapy water, no glue required)
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 21 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high feedrates.
Tune Pressure Advance (PA) / K-factor to approximately 0.024 via OrcaSlicer dynamic calibration for clean corners.
Configure nozzle temperature to 210°C for general layers and 215°C for the first layer to improve initial bed grab.
Enable Scarf Joint Seams under Quality settings to eliminate vertical surface zits at layer transitions.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting or warping on large prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PEI bed surface contaminated with oils or ambient room draft affecting the open-frame P1P chassis.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Wash the textured PEI sheet with warm water and dish soap, increase bed temperature to 62°C, and shield the printer from direct HVAC drafts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Fine wispy stringing during non-print travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Overture PLA+ has higher impact modifiers causing lower melt viscosity at prolonged travel delays.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2mm) in OrcaSlicer and ensure travel speed is set to 400 mm/s or higher.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Matte finish and weak layer bonding at maximum print speed
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Hotend heater unable to fully melt the core of the filament bead at sustained 21 mm³/s flow rates.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature by 5-10°C (up to 220°C) or reduce the max volumetric flow limit to 18 mm³/s.

faq.question: Does Overture PLA Professional require a hardened steel nozzle on the P1P?
faq.answer: No, Overture PLA Professional contains impact-modifying polymers rather than abrasive fibers, making the stock stainless steel nozzle completely suitable.

faq.question: Can I print Overture PLA Professional inside an enclosed P1P or should the chamber stay open?
faq.answer: Keep the chamber ventilated or top open if you have enclosed your P1P, as PLA Professional has a low glass transition temperature (~55°C) and can suffer heat creep.

faq.question: Do I need to dry Overture PLA Professional before printing?
faq.answer: While standard PLA+ is mildly hygroscopic, new vacuum-sealed spools print fine out of the box; dry at 45°C for 6 hours only if popping noises or excessive stringing occur.

faq.question: What is the recommended auxiliary part cooling fan setting on the P1P for this material?
faq.answer: Keep the auxiliary fan set between 40% and 70% to prevent uneven cooling shrinkage on the left side of the build plate.
